'''Julieta Dobles Yzaguirre''' (born 11 March 1943) is a Costa Rican poet, writer, and educator. She is a five-time winner of the [[Aquileo J. Echeverría National Prize]] and received the [[Magón National Prize for Culture]] in 2013.

==Biography==
Julieta Dobles Yzaguirre was born on 11 March 1943 in [[San José, Costa Rica|San José]], Costa Rica.<ref name="La Nación 21-01-2014">{{cite news |last1=Chaves Espinach |first1=Fernando |title=Julieta Dobles, la niña más grande de la poesía tica |url=https://www.nacion.com/viva/cultura/julieta-dobles-la-nina-mas-grande-de-la-poesia-tica/VIC2WWZNUZHXVIUVGWCBU2VDLU/story/ |access-date=23 December 2022 |work=La Nación |date=21 January 2014 |language=es}}</ref> Her mother, Ángela Yzaguirre, was a teacher and an unpublished poet.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Diez escritos reviven al Rubén Darío entrañable |trans-title=Ten writings resurrect the endearing Rubén Darío |url=https://www.nacion.com/viva/cultura/diez-escritos-reviven-al-ruben-dario-entranable/KYCLF2DNZVFBXJQADWIT6DUY4Q/story/ |access-date=7 December 2020 |work=La Nación |date=7 February 2016 |language=es-LA}}</ref> Dobles completed her studies at the [[University of Costa Rica]], where she studied [[philology]] and linguistics.<ref name="ticotimes">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Poet Julieta Dobles Yzaguirre wins Magón Award |url=https://ticotimes.net/2014/01/21/poet-julieta-dobles-yzaguirre-wins-magon-award |accessdate=18 July 2020 |work=[[The Tico Times]] |date=21 January 2014}}</ref> She also received a master's degree in Hispanic philology, specializing in Hispanic American literature, from [[Stony Brook University]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Rodríguez Chaverri |first1=Camilo |title=Julieta Dobles. Las Casas de su Memoria |url=http://www.artstudiomagazine.com/personajes/julieta-dobles.html |access-date=4 July 2019 |magazine=ArtStudio Magazine |date=15 September 2003 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190704022547/http://www.artstudiomagazine.com/personajes/julieta-dobles.html |archive-date=4 July 2019 |language=es-LA}}</ref> Following her education, she joined the ''Círculo de Poetas'' (Circle of Poets), where she was first taught by [[Jorge Debravo]] and [[Laureano Albán]].<ref name="La Nación 21-01-2014" />

In 1977, she signed the Transcendentalist Manifesto ({{langx|es|link=no|Manifiesto trascendentalista}}) alongside Laureano Albán, Carlos Francisco Monge and Ronald Bonilla.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Silva |first1=Carlos |title=Costa Rican Literature: Rich in Content and Still Flourishing |url=https://thecostaricanews.com/costa-rican-literature-rich-in-content-and-still-flourishing/ |work=The Costa Rica News |accessdate=4 July 2019 |date=14 September 2018}}</ref>{{Better source|date=July 2019}}

Doble's poems and articles have been published in various journals and magazines, including the poems ''Reloj de siempre'' (1965), ''El peso vivo'' (1968), ''Hojas furtivas'' (2007).<ref name="dircultura">{{cite web |title=Julieta Dobles Yzaguirre |url=https://www.dircultura.go.cr/premios-nacionales/cultura/2013/julieta-dobles-yzaguirre |website=Dirección de Cultura |publisher=Ministerio de Cultura y Juventud |access-date=7 December 2020 |language=es-CR |date=1 April 2019}}</ref> She is a professor of secondary education, as well as a professor of literature, communication, and language, at the Escuela de Estudios Generales at the [[University of Costa Rica]]. She has also coordinated various workshops on literature there. She has been a member of the [[Academia Costarricense de la Lengua]] since 2006.<ref name="ACL">{{cite web |title=Julieta Dobles Yzaguirre |url=https://www.acl.ac.cr/n_a.php?jdy |publisher=[[Academia Costarricense de la Lengua]] |accessdate=4 July 2019 |language=es-LA}}</ref>

==Awards==
Dobles is a five-time winner of the {{ill|Premio Nacional Aquileo J. Echeverría|es}} in Poetry (1968, 1977, 1992, 1997, and 2003). She was awarded the {{ill|Premio Editorial Costa Rica|es}} in 1975 and the runners-up' prize of the [[Premio Adonáis de Poesía]] in 1981.<ref name="La Nación 20-01-2014">{{cite news |last1=Miranda |first1=Yendry |title=Julieta Dobles es la ganadora del Premio Nacional de Cultura Magón 2013 |trans-title=Julieta Dobles is the winner of the 2013 Magón National Prize for Culture |url=http://www.nacion.com/ocio/literatura/Julieta-Dobles-Premio-Nacional-Cultura_0_1391660934.html |accessdate=4 July 2019 |work=La Nación |date=20 January 2014 |language=es-LA}}</ref> In 2013, the Costa Rican Ministry of Culture and Youth awarded Dobles the [[Magón National Prize for Culture]].<ref name="La Nación 21-01-2014" /><ref name="La Nación 20-01-2014" />

==Personal life==
Dobleswas married to poet [[Laureano Albán]] from 1967 to 2001.<ref name="La Nación 21-01-2014" /> They had five children, and worked on several books together.<ref name="La Nación 21-01-2014" /><ref name="ticotimes" />

==Bibliography==
Her published works include:<ref name="ACL" />
* ''Reloj de siempre'' (1965)
* ''El peso vivo'' (1968)
* ''Los pasos terrestres'' (1976)
* ''Hora de lejanías'' (1982)
* ''Los delitos de Pandora'' (1987)
* ''Una viajera demasiado azul'' (1990)
* ''Amar en Jerusalén'' (1992)
* ''Costa Rica poema a poema'' (1997)
* ''Poemas para arrepentidos'' (2003)
* ''Las casas de la memoria'' (2005)
* ''Fuera de álbum'' (2005)
* ''Hojas furtivas'' (2007)
* ''Cartas a Camila'' (with Laureano Albán, 2007)
* ''Trampas al tiempo'' (2015)
* ''Poemas del esplendor'' (2016)
